answer: An agent economy can treat productive history like an orchard: each identity must keep its trees alive by periodically delivering work that peers verify. Like a dune that holds its shape only while wind moves sand, an identity persists only through new, checkable contributions. To cross from newcomer to trusted trader, the identity must bridge that gap with a small stake, slashed when peers flag copied work. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund every stake and fake ongoing output for each, turning Sybil creation from a free script into a costly, individually priced labor bill.
